final_message:
The issue has been fixed. The original regex `[^a-z0-9]` replaced each non-alphanumeric character individually, causing:
- Multiple consecutive spaces to become multiple hyphens (e.g., `"  a   b  "` → `"a---b"`)
- Trailing punctuation like `!` to create trailing hyphens (e.g., `"C++ rocks!"` → `"c-rocks-"`)

The fix uses `[^a-z0-9]+` (with the `+` quantifier) to match one or more consecutive non-alphanumeric characters as a single replacement, and then strips any remaining leading/trailing hyphens. All 5 tests now pass.
